statement (modern): For a smooth projective complex surface, q(X)>0 implies the existence of a connected algebraic family of effective divisors whose members are not all linearly equivalent.
gap or error: Castelnuovo explicitly says Enriques's 1904 algebraic proof is inadequate; he does not provide a replacement here.
repair and reference: Use the smooth projective Picard variety and a Poincaré bundle twisted uniformly by a sufficiently ample line bundle; the projective bundle of sections gives the family. Grothendieck (1962), Exposé 236, Proposition 2.10(iii); Kleiman (2005), Theorems 5.4 and 5.11, Corollary 5.14. Full argument in commentary front matter.
notes: Source says the characteristic property is true at least with restrictions, citing Poincaré's transcendental research without a precise paper reference. Modern replacement assumes smooth projective over C. PDF5.

statement (modern): Conversely, a connected reduced algebraic family of effective divisors not contained in one complete linear system forces q(X)>0 for a smooth projective complex surface.
gap or error: Implicit in the source's description as a characteristic property; no proof is supplied.
repair and reference: The family's classifying map to Pic(X) cannot be constant. If q=0 then Pic(X) is discrete in characteristic zero and every map from a connected parameter space is constant. See commentary front matter and Kleiman (2005), §5.
notes: Connected family means a flat algebraic family of divisors; changing discrete degree components is excluded. PDF5.

statement (modern): Surface genera used in birational classification include birational invariants; in modern terms p_g, q, p_a=p_g-q, and the plurigenera P_m are invariant under birational maps of smooth projective complex surfaces.
gap or error: The preface describes the subject programmatically and does not name or define a complete list; no individual genus formula is proved here.
repair and reference: Blowup calculation and factorization of birational maps of smooth surfaces; H^1(O) and pluricanonical sections are unchanged. The cohomological companion in commentary supplies the argument. Hartshorne (1977), Chapter V, §§3, 5.
notes: Modern list is an explanatory expansion, not a claim that these symbols occur in the preface. K^2 is not invariant without a minimal-model convention. PDF5.

statement (modern): An irreducible affine surface in A^3 is given by f(x,y,z)=0; its projective hypersurface model in P^3 is given by a homogeneous equation F(x0,x1,x2,x3)=0.
notes: Opening convention. Integral/reduced and the algebraically closed characteristic-zero setting are made explicit in the commentary.

statement (modern): The order n of a projective hypersurface is its degree, equivalently the intersection number with a general line.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini, Book III, vol. II (1918), cited on p.1.
notes: Order is assumed, not developed in this extract.

statement (modern): The class of a surface, in the nondefective case, is the degree of its dual hypersurface.
gap or error: Dual-defective cases need a convention; the extract does not supply one.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini, Book III, vol. II (1918).
notes: Modern interpretation of an explicitly assumed projective notion, not a claim that every dual is a hypersurface.

statement (modern): A first polar of a homogeneous hypersurface F with respect to [a0:...:a3] has equation sum(ai ∂F/∂xi)=0.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini, Book III, vol. II (1918).
notes: The term polar surface is assumed here; its local use at pinch points occurs on p.8.

statement (modern): A point p of a degree-n hypersurface is smooth exactly when a general line through p has local intersection multiplicity one and n−1 residual intersections.
gap or error: The word general and intersection multiplicities must be supplied; tangent or contained lines are exceptions.
repair and reference: Use the first nonzero homogeneous term of the local equation, or the Jacobian criterion.
notes: Source describes the general line-intersection characterization.

statement (modern): A smooth surface germ admits formal/analytic coordinates (u,v), so every finite jet of the germ can be represented on a plane.
repair and reference: Implicit function theorem: f_z(p)≠0 gives z=g(x,y); equivalently completed local ring C[[u,v]].
notes: This does not assert Zariski local isomorphism to A^2 or rationality of the surface.

statement (modern): The first-order approximation to a smooth surface at p is its tangent plane.
repair and reference: The degree-one Taylor term df(p)=0 defines T_pX.
notes: Explicit first step of the local approximation argument.

statement (modern): After choosing the tangent plane z=0, the second-order approximation has equation z=g2(x,y), and vertical projection identifies this quadratic graph with its parameter plane.
repair and reference: Truncate the implicit-function expansion at degree two.
notes: Enriques writes z=φ2(xy). The scan agrees.

statement (modern): A curve germ at a smooth surface point has the same embedded local theory as a plane-curve germ and can be described using successive infinitely near points.
repair and reference: Local coordinates plus embedded resolution of plane curves; Enriques–Chisini, Book IV, vol. II, cited on p.2.
notes: The book imports the plane-curve singularity theory.

statement (modern): A point has multiplicity r>1 when a general line through it has intersection multiplicity r, leaving n−r residual intersections on a degree-n surface.
gap or error: Again the assertion is about general lines, not every line.
repair and reference: Expand f=f_r+f_{r+1}+... and substitute a general line direction.
notes: The residual count n−r agrees with the scan.

statement (modern): The singular locus may contain multiple curves, isolated multiple points, and exceptional higher singularities lying on a multiple curve.
repair and reference: Distinguish the one-dimensional and zero-dimensional strata of the singular locus and special points of the former.
notes: The three possibilities are explicitly distinguished.

statement (modern): At a general ordinary point of an r-fold curve, the surface has r smooth local branches with distinct tangent planes.
gap or error: Ordinary and general are essential; multiplicity r alone does not imply r smooth branches.
repair and reference: Interpret via local analytic branches or normalization. Enriques immediately discusses the special cases.
notes: The source itself uses “in generale,” so this is a qualification rather than a false universal theorem.

statement (modern): At an isolated multiplicity-r point, directions with intersection multiplicity at least r+1 form the degree-r projectivized tangent cone V(f_r) in P^2.
repair and reference: For direction v, substitute tv into f: the leading coefficient is f_r(v).
notes: The tangent cone is generally irreducible only under an additional generality assumption.

statement (modern): Branches along a multiple curve may become tangent or merge; a cuspidal double curve is the simplest named example of a single higher-order branch.
repair and reference: For example x^2−y^3=0 in A^3 has a cuspidal transverse section along the z-axis.
notes: This is an example of specialization, not part of the ordinary double-curve model.

statement (modern): The tangent cone of an isolated multiple point may be reducible or a plane with multiplicity r; a uniplanar double point has doubled-plane tangent cone.
repair and reference: The initial homogeneous form may factor, or be a power of a linear form.
notes: Tangent-cone support alone does not specify the analytic singularity type.

statement (modern): Infinitely near points are points on successive blowups; “infinitesimal curves” describe loci of such points above an original point.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini, Book IV, chapter IV, cited on p.2; modern interpretation through iterated blowups.
notes: The conjunction o in “proprie o infinitesime” is upright in the scan.

statement (modern): An ordinary uniplanar double point whose cubic term on the tangent plane has three distinct zeros has three distinct infinitely near ordinary double points after the first blowup.
gap or error: Printed wording omits the ordinary/generic cubic condition. A doubled tangent plane alone is insufficient.
repair and reference: Audit calculation: strict transform w^2+t g3(1,v)+... has singularities at the roots of g3. Counterexample z^2+x^3+y^4 has only one such point.
notes: Scan confirms the unqualified source sentence; this is a hypothesis repair, not OCR correction.

statement (modern): A surface tacnode has a general plane section with a double point followed by a double infinitely near point; the first blowup exhibits an infinitesimal double curve.
gap or error: General plane sections are intended; special sections can have worse behavior.
repair and reference: Audit example z^2+x^4+y^4: strict transform w^2+t^2(1+v^4)=0 is singular along the exceptional line.
notes: The source calls this the simplest infinitesimal double-line example.

statement (modern): A rational transformation is represented projectively by [φ0:φ1:φ2:φ3], or affinely by X=φ1/φ0, Y=φ2/φ0, Z=φ3/φ0.
repair and reference: Restrict to a nonempty domain of definition; rational maps are equivalence classes of such presentations.
notes: Displayed equation (1); verified against scan.

statement (modern): The projective coordinate forms of a rational map can be chosen homogeneous of one common degree.
repair and reference: Take common denominators and homogenize; cancel common divisorial factors.
notes: The wording about affine polynomials having the same order is properly understood projectively.

statement (modern): A dominant rational map P^3 ⇢ P^3 is generically finite; over characteristic zero a general target point has n distinct inverse images, where n is the function-field degree.
gap or error: Dominance and separability are needed for the finite distinct-point count.
repair and reference: Dimension theorem and finite separable extension C(P^3)⊂C(P^3).
notes: “Non degenere” supplies dominance in the intended setting.

statement (modern): The general fibers of a degree-n generically finite map form an order-n involution: a partition into n-point fibers.
gap or error: This is not necessarily a finite group action.
repair and reference: Interpret as the equivalence relation induced by the rational map.
notes: The book explicitly defines the classical term.

statement (modern): A surface not contracted by the rational map has a two-dimensional irreducible image, whose closure in P^3 is a hypersurface.
gap or error: The image need not have dimension two for a special contracted surface.
repair and reference: Use the dimension of the restriction and take reduced image closure.
notes: The source states the generic situation.

statement (modern): For a sufficiently general surface relative to the ambient finite correspondence, the restriction is birational onto its image; other points of the general ambient fiber lie off that surface.
gap or error: Generality relative to the correspondence is essential.
repair and reference: The off-diagonal fiber relation meets f×f in dimension at most one, so it does not identify the generic point of f.
notes: The “conjugate surface” records the other points in the ambient fibers.

statement (modern): If a surface is saturated by a subcorrespondence, the restriction can have degree m>1; its pushforward cycle is m times the reduced image.
gap or error: The scan prints “la trasformata di F” where the source surface is f.
repair and reference: Read “di f”; distinguish reduced image from pushforward cycle multiplicity.
notes: Enriques gives the cases m=n and m<n. This is not a nonreduced definition of the target surface itself.

statement (modern): A birational correspondence between two surfaces is distinct from a Cremona transformation of their ambient spaces; ambient extension is an additional property.
repair and reference: Intrinsic birationality is equality of surface function fields.
notes: Explicit footnote on p.3.

statement (modern): The chosen homogeneous coordinate presentation is undefined where all φi vanish; these points form its base locus.
gap or error: A common zero can be removable if the presentation has uncancelled common factors.
repair and reference: Use a presentation with fixed divisorial factors removed, and the intrinsic domain of definition.
notes: The source identifies common zeros with base points of the transforming system.

statement (modern): Resolving a genuine base point at a smooth surface point can replace it by an exceptional rational curve or a configuration of such curves.
gap or error: One arbitrary coordinate presentation does not automatically resolve the map; repeated blowups may be needed.
repair and reference: Bl_pX has exceptional P^1; resolve the base ideal by successive point blowups.
notes: The introductory term exceptional curve is refined in Chapter I.

statement (modern): Normalization or a suitable branch-separating modification separates the r local branches over a general ordinary r-fold curve point into r smooth points.
gap or error: Vanishing of arbitrary forms on the curve alone does not ensure branch separation.
repair and reference: Use normalization and a linear system that separates the branches.
notes: Source is explicitly generic; it is not a claim for cuspidal or tangent branches.

statement (modern): Blowing up an isolated ordinary multiple point replaces it by the projectivized tangent-cone curve, whose points represent first-order directions.
gap or error: A general suitable modification is intended; a singular tangent cone leaves further singularities.
repair and reference: Compute the strict transform in standard blowup charts.
notes: The source describes the ordinary case before noting the infinitely near complications.

statement (modern): Blowing up exposes first-neighbor points as proper points on the new surface; singularities may remain at those points or along exceptional curves.
repair and reference: Interpret the transformation in iterated blowup coordinates.
notes: This is the meaningful part of the claim about making infinitely near points proper.

statement (modern): The operation is said to simplify the infinitely near neighborhood by one stage, provided the transforming surfaces have no fixed tangent direction.
gap or error: “Reducing r to r−1 the neighborhood” does not define a decreasing invariant; interpreted as a decrease of multiplicity it is false.
repair and reference: Separate exposure of a neighbor level from multiplicity reduction; use a resolution theorem for termination. z^2+x^3+y^4 remains double after a blowup.
notes: The scan agrees with the ambiguous printed formulation; it should not be silently upgraded into a monotonicity theorem.

statement (modern): A sufficiently general map of a surface into P^3 can identify a one-dimensional family of distinct pairs and thereby create a double curve.
gap or error: Expected dimension is not guaranteed for every rational or Cremona map.
repair and reference: Apply the generic-projection theorem or a correctly saturated off-diagonal incidence calculation.
notes: The word “generally” matters.

statement (modern): In the chart φ0(p)φ0(q)≠0, equality of images is given by φi(p)φ0(q)−φi(q)φ0(p)=0 for i=1,2,3, together with f(p)=f(q)=0.
gap or error: Cross-multiplied equations outside the chart can contain extraneous base-locus components.
repair and reference: Work on the domain of definition before taking closure.
notes: All three equalities and both f equations agree with the scan.

statement (modern): The five equations in six variables have expected residual dimension one away from the two-dimensional diagonal p=q.
gap or error: Independence/proper intersection and removal of the diagonal are not proved by the count.
repair and reference: Use the off-diagonal fiber product and generic intersection; the residual locus can be empty in special cases.
notes: The equations x=x′, y=y′, z=z′ are the displayed trivial solutions.

statement (modern): For an ambient map of degree >1, its off-diagonal fiber correspondence is generically three-dimensional; two independent surface conditions then give a curve.
gap or error: The footnote presupposes a nonempty residual correspondence and proper intersections; the degree-one case can have none.
repair and reference: Take closure of the off-diagonal relation on the finite locus, then intersect with f×f.
notes: This is the separate six-dimensional ambient-space footnote argument.

statement (modern): Special transformations can identify more than two source points along a curve, producing a higher multiple curve in the image.
repair and reference: Use higher fiber products or local branch counts.
notes: A stated possibility, not a generic projection assertion.

statement (modern): A transformation may contract curves to isolated singularities, and special source or mapping configurations can produce more complicated target singularities.
gap or error: A contracted curve need not yield a singular point; a (−1)-curve may contract to a smooth point.
repair and reference: Read the sentence as a possibility. Chapter I gives the smooth contraction case.
notes: No artificial contradiction should be inferred by making this possibility universal.

statement (modern): Using r+1 rational coordinate sections defines a rational map to P^r with affine coordinates Xi=φi/φ0.
repair and reference: Homogenize the displayed expressions.
notes: The small raised mark in the first S_r label is retained diplomatically as S′_r; it has no mathematical effect.

statement (modern): The image closure is algebraic and may be realized as an irreducible component of an intersection of hypersurfaces in the target projective space.
repair and reference: Elimination theory; Enriques–Chisini, Book I, §23, cited in the footnote.
notes: “Partial intersection” does not assert that the image is a complete intersection.

statement (modern): The generic birationality and ordinary-branch-separation observations for maps to P^3 extend to suitable systems with more target coordinates.
gap or error: Generality and actual branch separation are required.
repair and reference: Use a base-ideal resolution followed by enough separating sections.
notes: The symbol r is reused for target dimension and branch multiplicity in the source; these should be distinguished.

statement (modern): For a suitably general map of a smooth surface, double-point identifications have expected dimension 4−r: none for r≥5, finitely many for r=4.
gap or error: Expected dimension alone neither ensures immersion nor excludes higher local singularities.
repair and reference: For embeddings, use secant and tangent avoidance; see the commentary proof.
notes: The source states the two threshold cases rather than this compact formula.

statement (modern): A smooth projective surface can be embedded in P^5 by general projection from a high-dimensional embedding, since a general center avoids all secant and tangent lines.
gap or error: The printed count explicitly discusses distinct pairs; tangent-direction separation also has to be supplied.
repair and reference: Secant closure has dimension ≤5; a center P^(N−6) avoids it and the induced morphism separates length-two subschemes.
notes: This proves the five-dimensional bound after resolution, not resolution itself.

statement (modern): Ordinary multiple curves and ordinary isolated points are locally resolved by separating branches and blowing up smooth projectivized tangent cones.
gap or error: For nonordinary tangent cones the first operation does not suffice.
repair and reference: Normalization plus explicit ordinary-point blowup calculation.
notes: The author says this easy case is not the difficult part of the theorem.

statement (modern): A resolution strategy separates local improvement of infinitely near singularities from control of new global identifications introduced by mapping back to three-space.
gap or error: This is a strategy, not a terminating algorithm proved here.
repair and reference: Use a projective resolution followed by a sufficiently high embedding; avoid identifying pairs and tangent directions.
notes: The two tasks are explicitly separated by the source.

statement (modern): The reduction problem by birational transformations of the entire ambient three-space is referred to Chisini (1921).
gap or error: The exact hypotheses and proof of the cited ambient theorem are not reproduced.
repair and reference: Enriques cites O. Chisini, La risoluzione delle singolarità delle superficie mediante trasformazioni birazionali dello spazio, Memorie Acc. Bologna (1921).
notes: Retain as an imported historical result, not a theorem independently proved in the extract.

statement (modern): The graph of a birational correspondence is smooth at a point where a graph projection is a local isomorphism to a smooth endpoint.
gap or error: The printed assertion that its singularities can occur only over singularities common to both endpoints is false for an arbitrary graph closure.
repair and reference: Audit counterexample: (x,y)↦(x²/y,x³/y²), whose graph is the singular twisted-cubic cone yX=x², yY=xX, xY=X², although both endpoints are planes. Resolve simultaneous indeterminacy.
notes: This is a mathematical qualification of the Levi graph remark, not a denial of the resolution theorem.

statement (modern): Every integral projective surface over C is birational to a smooth projective surface embedded in P^5.
gap or error: No proof of resolution is given here; the author explicitly says so.
repair and reference: Surface resolution, then the secant-avoidance embedding proof. Modern precise source: Lipman (1978), theorem p.151; Stacks Project, Theorem 54.14.5, Tag 0BGP.
notes: The scan reads qualsiansi, not the transcribed qualsiasi.

statement (modern): The resolution theorem is supported by references to Levi (1897), Chisini (1921), Albanese (1924), Walker (1935), and Zariski (1939; further 1941 pointer).
gap or error: The text credits Levi with a rigorous priority claim; this audit does not certify all historical proofs or priority from the extract.
repair and reference: Walker, Annals 36(2), 336–365, doi:10.2307/1968575; Zariski, Annals 40(3), 639–689, doi:10.2307/1968949. Both are already cited by Enriques.
notes: Not a claim that all these works are later repairs unknown to Enriques; modern proof dependencies are stated separately.

statement (modern): Starting with a smooth model in P^5, successive general projections to P^4 and then P^3 give a birational hypersurface model.
gap or error: Centers must avoid the surface and the relevant exceptional incidence loci.
repair and reference: Generic-projection theorem; ample pullback rules out contracted curves for the general finite map.
notes: The two centers together correspond to a general line center in P^5.

statement (modern): A general projected hypersurface model has an ordinary double curve, finitely many ordinary triple points, and finitely many pinch points.
gap or error: The complete local classification is stronger than the distinct-point dimension counts printed here.
repair and reference: Ciliberto–Flamini (2011), Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.5; for existence after re-embedding, the explicit jet argument in the commentary.
notes: “Singolarità normali” means ordinary singularities, not a normal variety.

statement (modern): For a nondegenerate surface in the stated projective setting, the family of general secant lines has dimension four.
gap or error: A plane or degenerate embedding is excluded; “always” must be read in the standing nondegenerate setup.
repair and reference: Pairs of general points give four parameters and a general secant meets the surface in finitely many points.
notes: Uses the trisecant principle to control generic fibers of the pair-to-line map.

statement (modern): A general point of P^5 lies on finitely many secants of a surface there if the secant variety fills P^5, and on none otherwise.
gap or error: Finite must allow zero; Veronese is the secant-defective case.
repair and reference: The secant point-line incidence has dimension five; apply the fiber-dimension theorem.
notes: No positive number of double points is asserted for every surface.

statement (modern): For a nondegenerate surface in P^4 with full secant variety, secants through a general point form a one-dimensional family.
repair and reference: Five-dimensional point-line incidence over a four-dimensional image.
notes: This accounts for the double curve in the next projection.

statement (modern): A general projection of a smooth surface from P^5 to P^4 has at most finitely many ordinary improper double points.
gap or error: Transversality and immersion require more than the parameter count.
repair and reference: Avoid the tangent locus and use generic transversality; Ciliberto–Flamini (2011), §2.2, Definition 2.3.
notes: The finite number may be zero.

statement (modern): The next general projection to P^3 produces a double curve; the images of the improper double points of the P^4 model lie on that curve.
repair and reference: Track the two normalization branches through the projection.
notes: These are not necessarily singular points of the reduced double curve.

statement (modern): Through a general line center L in P^5 there is a one-dimensional family of bisecant planes and a finite family of trisecant planes.
gap or error: Proper intersection and exclusion of more degenerate plane families are needed.
repair and reference: Planes through L containing a pair correspond to secants meeting L; triples span planes, with six containment conditions in G(2,5).
notes: Modern incidence interpretation of the source count.

statement (modern): The general secant of a nonplanar curve is not trisecant; this excludes all general surface secants being trisecants.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini, Book III, chapter IV, §43, vol.II, p.289; apply to a suitable hyperplane-section curve.
notes: The curve trisecant lemma is cited, not proved in the extract.

statement (modern): A general point of P^5 lies on no trisecant of the smooth surface; after projection to P^4 a general point lies on at most finitely many trisecants.
gap or error: The estimates concern general centers and nondegenerate section curves.
repair and reference: The trisecant-line family has dimension at most three; adjoining a point adds one dimension.
notes: The dimension bound justifies emptiness in P^5 and finite fibers in P^4.

statement (modern): General trisecant planes are not automatically quadrisecant; a general projection center line therefore avoids planes yielding four distinct preimages.
gap or error: This controls distinct points, not nonreduced fibers or tangency degeneracies.
repair and reference: Hyperplane-section reduction and inner projection to the curve trisecant lemma; bad planes have dimension ≤5, their contained-line incidence ≤7<dim G(1,5)=8.
notes: Enriques cites his 1936 Berzolari-volume paper, p.351.

statement (modern): Every surface is birational to a P^3 model with only ordinary singularities.
gap or error: The displayed proof omits local jet/transversality control, despite the phrase “rigorously demonstrated.”
repair and reference: Resolve; re-embed sufficiently positively; apply the detailed multi-jet calculation in the commentary, or the checked general-projection theorem.
notes: Attributed to Noether (1888), without a precise title on this page.

statement (modern): The source provisionally allows nodes (“incroci”) of the double curve, arising from special double secants of the projecting chord cone.
gap or error: Such nodes are absent in the strict modern ordinary model of a general projection; pp.10–11 subsequently attempt to exclude them.
repair and reference: Read as an interim possibility before the later exclusion, not a final generic singularity classification.
notes: A node of the double curve corresponds to a tacnodal configuration of surface branches in the subsequent argument.

statement (modern): There are finitely many pinch points where the two local branches along the double curve merge; locally the image is x²−y²z=0.
repair and reference: Normalization (u,v)↦(uv,u,v²); the double curve itself is smooth at the pinch point.
notes: “Cuspidal point” refers to the folding surface, not a cusp of the reduced double curve.

statement (modern): A pinch point is a simple base point of the variable residual curves cut by the polar surfaces after removal of the fixed double-curve component.
repair and reference: For F=x²−y²z the pullback of aFx+bFy+cFz is u(2av−2bv²−cu); the residual has an ordinary linear term at u=v=0.
notes: Explicit local proof supplied by this audit.

statement (modern): Birational surface theory can be carried out either on a smooth model in P^5 or on the smooth normalization of an ordinary P^3 model.
repair and reference: Combine resolution, projection, and the ordinary local normalizations.
notes: The singular image itself should not be substituted for the smooth model in cohomological invariants without normalization.

statement (modern): A general biplanar point of the double curve represents two distinct smooth points on the normalization, one for each local branch.
repair and reference: Normalize the local model xy=0 into the disjoint local branches.
notes: The analogy with the two branches of a nodal curve is exact.

statement (modern): Every birational class of surfaces has an ordinary P^3 model with irreducible double curve after a suitable choice of smooth embedding.
gap or error: The Veronese exception in a fixed embedding does not obstruct this existential statement.
repair and reference: Choose a sufficiently positive nondefective embedding, project to P^5, and apply the secant-incidence proof.
notes: This is the refinement announced at the beginning of §5.

statement (modern): The proof of double-curve irreducibility assumes the principles of linear systems developed later in the opening sections of Chapter I.
repair and reference: Use divisor line bundles, Bertini’s second theorem, and connectedness in a proper family.
notes: The author explicitly acknowledges this forward dependence.

statement (modern): An ordinary improper double point of a surface in P^4 is the image of two distinct smooth normalization points with independent tangent planes.
repair and reference: Modern formulation in Ciliberto–Flamini (2011), Definition 2.3.
notes: It is not a normal quadratic surface singularity.

statement (modern): For a nondegenerate surface in P^4 with only ordinary improper double points, a reducible double curve of the general projection to P^3 forces the surface to be a projected Veronese surface.
gap or error: The subsequent proof contains unproved specialization and dominance steps.
repair and reference: Franchetta (1941, 1947); modern statement Ciliberto–Flamini (2011), Theorem 2.6. The P^5 case has the replacement proof given below.
notes: Do not call the theorem false because its printed proof is compressed.

statement (modern): The Veronese surface v2(P²)⊂P^5 is the degree-four image of P² under the complete five-dimensional projective linear system of conics.
notes: The source gives both the degree and the conic-system description.

statement (modern): A three-dimensional family of distinct smooth pairs whose tangent planes meet in a line cannot have its joining secants fill P^4.
gap or error: The printed infinitesimal proof does not justify every fixed-hyperplane transition.
repair and reference: Audit differential proof: the secant evaluation has tangent image inside the common P³, hence generic rank≤3 and cannot dominate P^4 in characteristic zero.
notes: This is a rigorous proof of the exact lemma, without classifying developable families.

statement (modern): For a general fixed p in the alleged three-dimensional pair family, its possible partners q form at least a curve C.
gap or error: The projection of the pair family to the first surface must dominate; otherwise the dimension conclusion needs reformulation.
repair and reference: Restrict to a dominating irreducible incidence component and apply fiber dimension.
notes: Part of the lemma proof, not an independent global theorem about all tangent pairs.

statement (modern): The source argues that tangent planes along a partner curve C and the fixed tangent plane at p lie in one fixed P³.
gap or error: Passing from first-order containment at infinitely near q,q′ to one fixed hyperplane along all C is not justified in the short argument.
repair and reference: Avoid this integration step by the secant-evaluation rank proof of IN072.
notes: The desired non-filling conclusion is valid independently of this compressed subsidiary step.

statement (modern): The source next concludes that the contact curves C are planar, possibly lines, by intersecting neighboring common hyperplanes.
gap or error: Requires control that the relevant hyperplanes are distinct and vary as claimed.
repair and reference: The replacement rank argument proves the lemma without needing this classification step.
notes: Recorded separately because it is an explicit intermediate claim.

statement (modern): The alleged configuration would be ruled or carry a one-dimensional developable family of planes, and its relevant secants would not fill P^4.
gap or error: Classification of the possible plane families is abbreviated.
repair and reference: Use IN072’s differential proof for the required non-filling conclusion.
notes: The intraline determinato-dalla hyphen is present in the scan.

statement (modern): If the general projected double curve is reducible, its components have connected union.
gap or error: The argument uses normalization, linear-system connectedness, and absence of composition with a pencil.
repair and reference: Combine IN078–IN081; interpret the apparent divisors on a smooth model.
notes: Connectedness is not being inferred from reducibility alone.

statement (modern): A rationally or unirationally parametrized family of divisors on a smooth projective variety has constant Picard class and lies in a complete linear system.
gap or error: The parameter-to-Picard map and pullback to a smooth model are implicit.
repair and reference: A rational map from P^n to an abelian variety is constant; Enriques–Chisini, Book V, chapter I, §9, pp.78,485.
notes: This is the source’s cited extension from divisors on curves to varieties.

statement (modern): If a linear system has general integral member, every member has connected support.
