statement (modern): For a net the pencil of members through P has all n points of the generic map fiber as base points.
repair and reference: Two independent section equations cut that fiber on the resolved moving surface.

statement (modern): The branch curve of a multiple plane parametrizes fibers with coincident points.
gap or error: Simple double ramification is only a generic situation for a suitable net; arbitrary nets may ramify more highly.
repair and reference: Use the discriminant of the finite Stein factor over P^2.

statement (modern): Cones of order a with common external vertex cut a system on a degree-m surface that is composed with a degree-m projection.
gap or error: Vertex must be external/general for degree m; a>=2 gives dimension at least3.
repair and reference: Projection from vertex followed by degree-a Veronese map.

statement (modern): The effective degree of that cone system is m a^2 (Enriques prints mn with n=a).
gap or error: Genuine printed formula error: scan has mn, missing square.
repair and reference: M=aH and H^2=m, so M^2=ma^2; image is Veronese surface of degree a^2.
notes: This is not a transcription error.

statement (modern): A simple system is a system giving a birational map onto its image.
repair and reference: Equivalently the associated involution has generic degree1.

statement (modern): For equations sum(lambda_i phi_i)=0, the image coordinates are [phi0:...:phir].
gap or error: The symbols X_i=phi_i are homogeneous coordinates up to one common nonzero scalar.
repair and reference: Coordinate form of the evaluation map.

statement (modern): Birational geometry with a specified simple system is represented by projective geometry of its image.
gap or error: Must retain the specified system; no assertion that all birational models are projectively equivalent.
repair and reference: A basis change gives a projectivity, and a projectivity of birational images lifts to the birational identification.

statement (modern): An inclusion of section spaces W subset V corresponds to projection of the V-image onto the W-image.
repair and reference: Projection center is P(ker(V^vee-->W^vee)).

statement (modern): Imposed isolated base conditions appear as the center intersecting the image in points, with appropriate scheme structure.
gap or error: Set-theoretic points alone lose multiplicity and infinitely near information.
repair and reference: Interpret the intersection as the base ideal on the normalized/resolved model.

statement (modern): When a subsystem is obtained by adding a fixed curve L, that curve lies in the projection center.
repair and reference: All its representing sections vanish along L.

statement (modern): At an i-fold smooth base point with no fixed tangent, restriction to the first exceptional P^1 has line-bundle degree i.
repair and reference: Leading homogeneous forms are sections of O_P1(i), and the resolved moving class has intersection i with E.

statement (modern): The image exceptional curve has degree i if and only if the restriction to E has degree1.
gap or error: The text asserts degree i without this extra restriction; global birationality is insufficient.
repair and reference: Always deg(E-->image E) times deg(image E)=i. Explicit birational map [x²z:y²z:x³:y³] maps E twice onto a line; commentary I.6.

statement (modern): For one simple infinitely near point after an i-fold base point, the strict first exceptional component has moving intersection i-1, and the second has intersection1.
gap or error: These are image degrees only after accounting for mapping degrees and any extra contracted components.
repair and reference: M=pi*D-iE0*-E1, E0 prime=E0*-E1; direct intersection computation.

statement (modern): When i=1 in that two-point cluster, the first strict exceptional curve is a contracted (-2)-curve and the second maps to a line.
gap or error: To identify the image as an ordinary double point one must choose a normal model contracting only that (-2)-curve.
repair and reference: The standard contraction gives A1:ab=c²; the image line passes through its vertex.

statement (modern): An arbitrary fixed singularity/base cluster can be resolved by successive point blowups, producing an exceptional divisor governed by proximity data.
gap or error: This page cites the theory without proving it.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini,BookIV,volII,pp327ff.; Barber–Zariski1935; Du Val1936; modern point-blowup cluster construction.

statement (modern): The number of exceptional components cannot in general be identified with the number of analytic branches of a general curve germ.
gap or error: The printed wording uses branches imprecisely and does not specify the resolution or subsequent contractions.
repair and reference: Components of a smooth resolution are indexed by blowup centers; one ordinary multiple point has several branches but one first exceptional component; y²=x⁵ has one branch and repeated blowups.

statement (modern): Exceptional incidence and multiplicities encode the proximity relations of the infinitely near points.
repair and reference: Enriques–Chisini reference and Barber–Zariski1935; see ChapterI§§11–12 for the source development.
notes: Printed E.Barber should be S.F.Barber; Mathematik is a printed journal-name error.

statement (modern): Two effective divisors are linearly equivalent exactly when they lie in a common linear system.
gap or error: Enriques uses the symbol equivalent or =; this is linear, not numerical, equivalence.
repair and reference: C~K iff C-K=div(t).

statement (modern): Two distinct linearly equivalent members span a pencil; dimension zero handles a divisor equivalent to itself.
repair and reference: Span their defining sections, or the single section in the identical case.

statement (modern): Linearly equivalent divisors have the same projective degree.
gap or error: Equal degree is not sufficient for equivalence.
repair and reference: Intersection of a principal divisor with a hyperplane is zero.

statement (modern): Equivalent curves can be realized as zero and pole members of a rational function; reciprocation exchanges them.
gap or error: Cancel any common components before speaking of the actual zero and pole divisors.
repair and reference: If div(t)=C-K, then div(1/t)=K-C.

statement (modern): Linear equivalence is reflexive.
repair and reference: Use the constant rational function1.

statement (modern): Linear equivalence is symmetric.
repair and reference: Use reciprocal rational functions.

statement (modern): Linear equivalence is transitive.
repair and reference: With div(t)=K-C and div(tau)=K-L, div(tau/t)=C-L; the text has the correct quotient sign.

statement (modern): All effective divisors equivalent to C form one complete linear system.
gap or error: The rational-function construction presupposes finite dimensionality; supplied uniformly by proper coherent cohomology.
repair and reference: |C|=P H^0(X,O_X(C)); commentary I.7 proves the divisor-section correspondence.

statement (modern): The complete system is constructed by linear combinations of rational functions with poles bounded by C.
gap or error: Exactly equal pole divisor is not a vector-space condition; bounded poles is the precise meaning.
repair and reference: Use L(C) and identify nonzero functions up to scalar.

statement (modern): A complete system is not necessarily base-point-free; the book uses a general/virtual convention rather than proving universal freedom from base points.
gap or error: Reading in general as always would be false.
repair and reference: Cubics through eight general plane points give a complete pencil on their blowup with a ninth base point.

statement (modern): Completeness can be defined relative to an assigned cluster of base points and multiplicities.
repair and reference: Use all sections of the line bundle satisfying the cluster ideal, or H^0(pi*D-sum m_iE_i*) on its blowup.

statement (modern): Transforming base points into exceptional curves requires removing their exceptional contributions from total transforms to obtain the moving system.
repair and reference: Distinguish pi*D from strict transform pi*D-sum m_iE_i*.

statement (modern): An irreducible complete relative system is maximal among systems containing a given at least two-dimensional subsystem with the same moving degree and base data.
gap or error: Same degree means effective degree with the assigned base conditions retained.
repair and reference: Complete the corresponding fixed divisor class on the resolved model.

statement (modern): Any member determines the same complete system.
repair and reference: If C prime~C then O(C prime) is isomorphic to O(C); transitivity.

statement (modern): Successive enlargement of a fixed section space terminates at the unique complete space.
gap or error: The printed degree bound applies only to irreducible moving systems; use finite h^0 in general.
repair and reference: Ascending chains of subspaces of H^0(X,L) terminate.

statement (modern): An intrinsically normal projective model is one whose hyperplane series on the abstract normalized model is complete, hence admits no further same-degree lift by adding sections.
gap or error: Not the modern local-ring normality condition; for nonnormal F also not merely surjectivity onto H^0(F,O_F(1)).
repair and reference: Intrinsic completeness on the normalization; on a smooth embedded surface this is linear normality.

statement (modern): Completing a fixed polarized model by adjoining sections gives a projectively unique final model.
gap or error: Keep the birational model and hyperplane line bundle fixed.
repair and reference: Any two bases of the full H^0(L) differ by GL(H^0(L)).

statement (modern): Two distinct incomplete same-degree lifts may fail to be projectively equivalent yet admit the same final complete lift.
repair and reference: They correspond to different intermediate subspaces of the same complete section space.

statement (modern): The complete system of cubics through four general plane points has projective dimension5, self-intersection5, and sectional genus1.
gap or error: General-position hypothesis on the four points is implicit.
repair and reference: On Bl_4 P² use D=3H-sum E_i=-K, h^0=10-4=6, D²=5, adjunction gives genus1.

statement (modern): That complete system embeds the degree-five del Pezzo surface in P^5.
repair and reference: Enriques–Conforto1939(1945), as cited; modern verified Bauer–Catanese2021,section2.

statement (modern): A four-dimensional section subspace giving a P^3 image lies in a one-parameter family of five-dimensional subspaces giving P^4 images.
repair and reference: If dim H^0(D)=6 and dim V=4, intermediate W have W/V a line in H^0(D)/V, parametrized by P^1.

statement (modern): The intermediate projected quintics are generally projectively inequivalent but have the same complete anticanonical lift.
gap or error: Birationally distinct refers to systems, not the underlying rational surfaces; exceptional coincidences are not excluded by the text.
repair and reference: The polarized automorphism group is finite S5 (Bauer–Catanese2021); distinct generic subspaces are inequivalent.

statement (modern): The ordinary general P^3 projection has a double curve of degree5, lying on a quadric cone, and one ordinary triple point at the cone vertex.
gap or error: The spatial singularity computation is not supplied and requires a general ordinary projection.
repair and reference: Commentary I.7 reconstructs Delta=2D,deg B=5,p_a(B)=2,8pinches,1triple via conductor and Thom–Porteous; unique quadric is singular at the triple point and cannot split by reduced-conductor odd-degree parity.

statement (modern): Adding linearly equivalent pairs gives linearly equivalent sums.
repair and reference: Multiplication of rational functions: div(t tau)=div(t)+div(tau).

statement (modern): The complete sum of two systems is the full system of their tensor-product divisor class, |C+K|.
repair and reference: All composed divisors C prime+K prime lie in the same class.

statement (modern): Two positive-dimensional systems with integral general members, not the same pencil, have an irreducible general complete sum.
gap or error: Retain assigned base conditions if relative completeness is intended.
repair and reference: Product map followed by Segre has surface image; apply Bertini irreducibility.

statement (modern): Prescribed base conditions persist in a relative complete sum.
gap or error: False for an unrestricted complete divisor class; assigned is essential.
repair and reference: Retain the cluster ideal; two pencils of lines through different plane points have unrestricted sum |2H|, which has no base point.

statement (modern): A positive multiple of an irreducible moving system that is not a pencil is generically irreducible.
gap or error: The pencil exception is lack of guarantee, not an assertion that all unrestricted multiples of a pencil are reducible.
repair and reference: The multiple system contains a system with surface image; Bertini.

statement (modern): The minimal sum is the smallest linear subsystem containing all pairwise sums of members.
repair and reference: P image(V tensor W-->H^0(L tensor N)).

statement (modern): The minimal sum may be strictly smaller than the complete sum.
repair and reference: Multiplication of sections need not be surjective; the quadric example follows.

statement (modern): Hyperplanes through a smooth point O of a spatial surface of degree at least2 give a complete relative net.
gap or error: For a plane the induced system drops dimension.
repair and reference: Ambient linear forms through O give vector dimension3; hypersurface restriction and evaluation at O.

statement (modern): The minimal double of that net is cut by quadratic cones with vertex O and has projective dimension5.
gap or error: For degree at least2, restriction of the cone forms is injective; the following strict-containment claim needs degree at least3.
repair and reference: Sym² of a3-dimensional section space has dimension6; forms in the three coordinates vanishing at O.

statement (modern): The complete relative double is cut by quadrics tangent to F at O and has projective dimension6 for degree(F)>=3.
gap or error: The text omits degree>=3; on a smooth quadric the surface equation reduces this to dimension5 and the minimal double is already complete.
repair and reference: Three first-jet conditions in the10-dimensional quadric space leave7 sections; account for restriction kernel.

statement (modern): The residual system to a fixed effective K in a system consists of divisors L with L+K a member.
repair and reference: Inverse image under multiplication by the canonical section s_K.

statement (modern): If a member of the complete |C| contains K, every K prime~K is contained in a member of |C|.
gap or error: Completeness is required.
repair and reference: For any L~C-K effective, L+K prime~C.

statement (modern): The complete residual system |C-K| depends only on the linear-equivalence class of K.
gap or error: The shortened italic wording omits complete, but the preceding paragraph assumes it; not true for arbitrary incomplete subsystems.
repair and reference: O(C-K prime) is isomorphic to O(C-K); multiplication identifies the residual space.

statement (modern): The complete difference is characterized by |L|=|C-K| and |C|=|L+K| when effective residues exist.
repair and reference: Equality of divisor classes and their complete systems.

statement (modern): Adjoint surfaces of fixed degree passing through the double curve of an ordinary spatial surface cut a complete residual system.
gap or error: Explicitly announced for later proof, not proved on p.28; requires the ordinary/conductor ideal convention.
repair and reference: Exact sequence0-->O_P3(e-d)-->I_B(e)-->nu_*O_X(eH-Delta)-->0, plus H¹(P³,O(k))=0; commentary I.8.

statement (modern): On a smooth hypersurface in P^3, all sections of O_F(e) are cut by degree-e ambient hypersurfaces.
repair and reference: Hypersurface restriction exact sequence and H¹(P³,O(e-d))=0; Stacks Tag01XS.

statement (modern): Every member in one complete residual class is residual to every member in the complementary class inside the complete adjoint system.
gap or error: Conditional on the stated completeness of ambient adjoint cuts.
repair and reference: Intrinsic residual theorem plus the projective complement.

statement (modern): Noether Restsatz comprises two distinct assertions: intrinsic residual invariance and completeness of the ambient adjoint cuts.
repair and reference: Enriques explicitly distinguishes these, citing Noether Math.Ann.VIII, Brill–NoetherVII, and Enriques–Chisini BookV.

statement (modern): The difference of an irreducible complete system and an effective divisor may have reducible general member.
repair and reference: On P¹xP¹, |(1,2)| minus (1,0) leaves |(0,2)|, a sum of two fibers.

statement (modern): If |L| is a base-point-free pencil with connected fibers, |2L| consists of sums of two fibers.
gap or error: Connected fibers are needed to identify the full section space with H^0(P¹,O(2)); primitive pencil is the intended case.
repair and reference: Projection formula and f_*O_X=O_P1.

statement (modern): A residual system can acquire a fixed component that was not fixed in the original system.
repair and reference: On Bl_p P², |H| minus a member of |H-E| leaves the fixed system |E|.

statement (modern): A residual system can acquire new base points outside the old base locus.
repair and reference: On Bl_8 P², subtract a suitable effective K from sufficiently ample |nA| so that the residue is the complete anticanonical cubic pencil, with a ninth base point.

statement (modern): Blowing up a newly created base point makes its contribution a fixed exceptional component in the total pullback of the residual system.
gap or error: The moving strict transform subtracts that exceptional multiplicity.
repair and reference: Total versus strict transforms of divisors under point blowup.

statement (modern): A difference |C-K| has an effective member only if a divisor in |C| contains a representative of K.
repair and reference: Equivalent to h^0(O(C-K))>0.

statement (modern): A virtual curve is a formal difference of effective divisor classes, meaningful even when its complete system is empty.
repair and reference: Modern Picard-group/divisor-class interpretation.

statement (modern): C-K is linearly equivalent to L-M iff C+M is linearly equivalent to K+L.
repair and reference: Group completion/cancellation in Pic(X).

statement (modern): Adding a sufficiently ample effective divisor makes any fixed virtual class effective.
gap or error: Sufficiently ample means mA for an ample A and m sufficiently large, not merely large self-intersection.
repair and reference: Ample twist global generation and Serre vanishing; Stacks Lemma30.17.1,Tag0B5U; commentary I.8.

statement (modern): Equivalent virtual classes have equivalent effective translates wherever those translates exist.
repair and reference: Tensor the corresponding isomorphic line bundles by O(D).

statement (modern): D+(C-K)=D+C-K in the divisor class group.
repair and reference: Associativity; the final colon in the scan is punctuation, not part of the equality.

statement (modern): A narrower virtual-class notion consists of noneffective classes with an effective positive multiple.
gap or error: This is strictly narrower than arbitrary formal differences.
repair and reference: Compare -H on P² with torsion-twisted line bundles on E x P¹; explicit calculation in commentary I.8.

statement (modern): Enriques traces the idea of noneffective canonical/virtual curves to his1893–1896 work, including genus-zero situations.
gap or error: Historical attribution in the supplied text; the original1896 canonical-class discussion was not fully reread.
repair and reference: Preserve source attribution and do not claim an independently established priority result.

statement (modern): Virtual classes have virtual degree and genus even without effective representatives, and can have an effective double.
gap or error: Definitions are deferred to ChapterIsection10.
repair and reference: Intersection-theoretic characters and Riemann–Roch/adjunction as developed in the later-section audit.

statement (modern): The term virtual curve is attributed to Severi1905, and its two-dimensional-cycle interpretation to Lefschetz.
gap or error: The exact Severi paper and Lefschetz passage were not directly read in this audit.
repair and reference: Enriques citation: Severi,Sulle curve algebriche virtuali appartenenti ad una superficie algebrica,Rend.Ist.Lombardo1905; modern topological map is c1:Pic(X)-->H²(X,Z).

statement (modern): The topological cycle class of a virtual divisor does not recover its linear-equivalence class.
gap or error: This is a necessary modern qualification, not a claim proved on this page.
repair and reference: Classes in Pic^0 map to zero under c1; distinguish divisor classes from all topological two-cycles.

statement (modern): For systems V⊂H⁰(L), W⊂H⁰(M), the minimum sum is P(im(V⊗W→H⁰(L⊗M))); the complete sum uses H⁰(L⊗M).
repair and reference: Commentary I.9 gives the multiplication-of-sections formulation.
notes: The two choices of sum are expressly allowed; K is an auxiliary curve class, not the canonical class.

statement (modern): For the general two-system construction, the sum has a surface image in P^R with R>r+s.
gap or error: The printed 'in generale' must be retained. A common pencil can give a curve image and equality R=r+s.
repair and reference: The family of decomposable sums has dimension r+s by unique factorization into two integral components. Bertini gives an irreducible general member of the minimum sum when its joint image is a surface, so the decomposable family is proper and R>r+s. Commentary I.9. Common-pencil exception gives equality.
notes: Not an unqualified theorem for every pair of irreducible systems.

statement (modern): Fixing K₀, the subsystem K₀+|C| consists of r-dimensional hyperplanes through a P^(R−r−1) containing the image of K₀.
gap or error: The ambient S_r in this paragraph is printed incorrectly; S_R is required.
repair and reference: The subspace k₀V has vector dimension r+1, so its annihilator has projective dimension R−r−1. Commentary I.9.
notes: The source slip is scan-verified, transcription line 1090.

statement (modern): Fixing C₀, the dual subsystem C₀+|K| has hyperplanes through a P^(R−s−1) containing C₀.
repair and reference: Apply the same annihilator calculation to c₀W. Commentary I.9.
notes: Reciprocal half of the preceding construction.

statement (modern): For C₀,K₀ without a common component, the two centers lie in one hyperplane and meet in P^(R−r−s−1).
gap or error: The source interchanges C and K when naming the two fixed curves in this sentence.
repair and reference: k₀V∩c₀W=C·c₀k₀; hence dim(k₀V+c₀W)=r+s+1. Commentary I.9.
notes: This proves the exact center dimension and identifies the intended labels.

statement (modern): Projection from that common center yields the subsystem k₀V+c₀W and a map to P^(r+s).
repair and reference: Coordinates [cᵢk₀,c₀kⱼ] give the asserted projection; Commentary I.9.
notes: Enriques performs the projective dimension calculation.

statement (modern): Under this projection, K₀ lies in P^(s−1) and C₀ in P^(r−1).
repair and reference: Take the quotient of each center by their common projective subspace; Commentary I.9.
notes: These dimensions confirm the correction to the preceding switched names.

statement (modern): Hyperplanes through the first projected fixed subspace cut the C-system; hyperplanes through the other cut the K-system.
repair and reference: The coordinates are sections divisible respectively by k₀ and c₀; remove the fixed divisor.
notes: The fixed components must be removed when interpreting the residual systems.

statement (modern): For r=2,s=1, the image lies in P³: the C-net is cut by planes through O and the K-pencil by planes through a line a not containing O.
repair and reference: Use [c₀k₀:c₁k₀:c₂k₀:c₀k₁]; O=[0:0:0:1], a={x₀=x₃=0}. Commentary I.9.
notes: A net means projective dimension two.

statement (modern): The net–pencil image is birational when the two systems do not factor through a common nontrivial generic finite correspondence.
gap or error: The historical word involuzione does not mean an automorphism of order two.
repair and reference: On c₀k₀≠0 the coordinates recover cᵢ/c₀ and kⱼ/k₀; birationality is equality of the generated field with C(X). Commentary I.9.
notes: Separability is automatic over C.

statement (modern): The same image is obtained by projectively identifying the net and pencil with the indicated stars of planes.
repair and reference: This is the same coordinate construction expressed geometrically. Commentary I.9.
notes: No additional existence theorem is needed once bases of V and W are chosen.

statement (modern): The fixed K₀ is contracted to O, whose multiplicity in the generic image is i=C·K.
gap or error: Requires the generic transverse setup and the birationality condition already stated.
repair and reference: A general plane through O has i intersections with the contracted neighborhood; equivalently use the transformed divisor on the blowup. Commentary I.9.
notes: O need not be smooth when the contracted K₀ has positive genus.

statement (modern): The fixed C₀ maps to a line a with multiplicity n=C² in the surface image.
repair and reference: A plane through a has residual K-image of degree i; the total plane-section degree is n+i. Commentary I.9.
notes: n is the resolved degree of the net.

statement (modern): The plane Oa cuts the image outside a in i exceptional lines through O.
gap or error: Repeated or infinitely near intersections require multiplicity-aware interpretation.
repair and reference: Blow up the transverse intersection scheme C₀∩K₀; each exceptional divisor has degree one under the transformed four-section system. Commentary I.9.
notes: The plane is x₀=0 in the displayed coordinates.

statement (modern): The birational image surface has degree n+i.
gap or error: For a map of degree d, the formula is d·deg(image)=n+i.
repair and reference: D=π*(C+K)−ΣEⱼ has D²=n+i because C²=n, K²=0, C·K=i. Commentary I.9.
notes: The source's birationality hypothesis is essential.

statement (modern): This image is defined by a projective three-dimensional subsystem of |C+K| with i base points at C₀∩K₀.
repair and reference: The vector space k₀V+c₀W has dimension four; its local base ideal at a transverse intersection is (c₀,k₀). Commentary I.9.
notes: Counts scheme length i, or i distinct points in the generic case.

statement (modern): Those base points account for the exceptional lines of the image model.
repair and reference: On each blowup exceptional Eⱼ, D|Eⱼ=O_P¹(1). Commentary I.9.
notes: This connects the base scheme and the projective picture.

statement (modern): Quadrics through a point O and a disjoint line a form a projective five-dimensional system.
repair and reference: h⁰(I_(O∪a)(2))=10−1−3=6; six independent products of the indicated plane equations span it. Commentary I.9.
notes: The dimension refers to ambient quadrics.

statement (modern): Restricting those quadrics to the image and removing fixed parts realizes the minimum sum of the net and pencil.
gap or error: The restricted system may have a relation if the surface itself is a quadric.
repair and reference: Use the multiplication map of section spaces; do not infer intrinsic projective dimension five merely from the ambient count. Commentary I.9.
notes: No source error is alleged in this dimension distinction.

statement (modern): For two systems on the same resolved model, (C₁+C₂)²=C₁²+C₂²+2C₁·C₂, hence n=n₁+n₂+2i.
gap or error: All degrees and intersections must use the same assigned-base-point convention.
repair and reference: Bilinearity of the intersection form; Beauville (1996), chap. I; Commentary I.10.
notes: The displayed polynomial identity and its numerical restatement are one claim.

statement (modern): The arithmetic genus of a sum is p_a(C₁+C₂)=p_a(C₁)+p_a(C₂)+C₁·C₂−1.
gap or error: Geometric genera agree only for smooth representatives on the resolved model; flat continuity preserves arithmetic genus.
repair and reference: Derive from p_a(D)=1+(D²+K_X·D)/2 or from Euler characteristics. Vakil (2002), class 6 §2; Commentary I.10.
notes: Enriques attributes the formula to Noether and cites Enriques–Chisini, book V, vol. III, p. 399.

statement (modern): The virtual degree of an isolated C is N−m−2i, using an auxiliary K with N=(C+K)², m=K², i=C·K.
repair and reference: This equals the intrinsic self-intersection C²; Commentary I.10.
notes: An isolated curve still defines a zero-dimensional complete linear system.

statement (modern): An auxiliary |K| can be chosen such that both |K| and |C+K| have irreducible general members.
gap or error: The words 'easily' conceal a sufficiently-positive twisting argument.
repair and reference: Take K=mH−C for m≫0 with K and mH very ample; use Serre vanishing and Bertini. Stacks Project, Tag 0B5U; Commentary I.10.
notes: This is a valid positivity theorem, not evidence of a false result.

statement (modern): The systems |(C+K₁)+K₂| and |(C+K₂)+K₁| represent the same total sum.
repair and reference: Associativity of tensor product / addition of divisor classes, with a common complete sum for the numerical comparison.
notes: The equality is used in the independence proof.

statement (modern): Computing that common degree in the two orders gives n₁=n₂, so virtual degree is independent of the auxiliary.
repair and reference: Expand N=(n₁+m₁+2i₁)+m₂+2j+2i₂ and its symmetric expression; cancel. Commentary I.10.
notes: The cancellation is written out in the source and is sound.

statement (modern): Virtual genus of an isolated curve is defined by inverting the genus-of-sum formula.
repair and reference: p_a(C)=p_a(C+K)−p_a(K)−C·K+1; Commentary I.10.
notes: The modern invariant is arithmetic genus, not normalization genus.

statement (modern): Virtual genus is independent of the chosen auxiliary.
repair and reference: Expand p_a(C+K₁+K₂) symmetrically as in Commentary I.10.
notes: The source says the proof is entirely similar rather than writing it out.

statement (modern): Virtual degree and genus remain defined for multiple curves and reducible curves with multiple components.
repair and reference: Use C² and 1+(C²+K_X·C)/2 for the Cartier divisor scheme, including its multiplicities. Commentary I.10.
notes: For mC, p_a(mC)=1+m(p_a(C)−1)+m(m−1)C²/2.

statement (modern): Virtual degree and genus also apply to a formal difference C−K whether or not it is effective.
repair and reference: Interpret it in Pic(X), with numerical polynomial p_a(D); Commentary I.10.
notes: This extends the virtual-curve construction from §8.

statement (modern): A formal difference can be made part of an irreducible positive system by adding a sufficiently positive L; its recovered characters are independent of L.
repair and reference: Twist by mH and use the same symmetric cancellation; Stacks Project, Tag 0B5U; Commentary I.10.
notes: No effectivity of C−K itself is asserted.

statement (modern): Birationally invariant interpretation of virtual characters requires specifying whether exceptional components are retained and which points are assigned.
gap or error: Self-intersection of the bare strict transform is not birationally invariant.
repair and reference: Use total transforms, or a fixed assigned cluster D'=π*D−ΣmᵢEᵢ*. Commentary I.10.
notes: Enriques explicitly discusses the choice rather than asserting unconditional invariance.

statement (modern): For a simple point on C, blowing it up gives total transform C̃+E and strict transform C̃.
gap or error: The displayed C̄+o assumes multiplicity one; a multiplicity-m point requires C̃+mE.
repair and reference: π*C=C̃+mE. Beauville (2020), Lecture II; Commentary I.10.
notes: A local illustrative omission of multiplicity must not be propagated to singular points.

statement (modern): If the point is an assigned base point, the transformed moving system omits the exceptional fixed contribution.
repair and reference: Subtract the prescribed base multiplicity before taking the moving transform.
notes: This is the strict transform for a general member of the assigned multiplicity.

statement (modern): If the point is not assigned, the total transformed system contains E+C̃ as the special member through the point.
repair and reference: Pull back the complete divisor class; a section vanishing at p acquires its exceptional component.
notes: The total class preserves square and arithmetic genus.

statement (modern): A point of actual multiplicity at least i may be assigned only virtual multiplicity i.
repair and reference: The class π*C−iE retains (m−i)E when the actual multiplicity is m>i; Commentary I.10; Casas-Alvero (2000), chap. 4.
notes: This may produce a virtual or reducible divisor, not the reduced strict transform.

statement (modern): Omitting a prescribed multiplicity-i condition increases virtual arithmetic genus by i(i−1)/2 for that blowup.
gap or error: It is not the total delta invariant of every multiplicity-i singularity; further infinitely near singularities contribute further drops.
repair and reference: Adjunction and K_Y=π*K_X+E give p_a(C̃)=p_a(C)−i(i−1)/2. Commentary I.10.
notes: Example y²=x⁵ has first drop 1 and total delta 2.

statement (modern): Omitting a multiplicity-i base condition increases self-intersection by i².
gap or error: The complete local intersection of two multiplicity-i curves can exceed i² if their tangents agree.
repair and reference: First-blowup formula C̃₁·C̃₂=C₁·C₂−i²; iterate for the remaining infinitely near intersection. Commentary I.10.
notes: This is exact for virtual degree; equality with total local contribution needs the tangent qualification.

statement (modern): An exceptional curve corresponds under a birational transformation to the full neighborhood of a smooth point.
gap or error: Merely being one component mapped to a point is weaker.
repair and reference: Use the entire exceptional fiber; §12 distinguishes it from individual components. Stacks Project, Tag 0C2I; Commentary I.11.
notes: Contraction to a singular point is a different notion.

statement (modern): An irreducible first-kind exceptional curve is contracted to a smooth point without base points on the curve.
gap or error: The full-neighborhood interpretation must be retained.
repair and reference: On a smooth surface it is a smooth P¹ with self-intersection −1. Stacks Project, Tag 0C2I.
notes: The definition is geometric; its numerical converse is stated later on p. 36.

statement (modern): A second-kind exceptional curve is transformed to a smooth-point neighborhood by a birational transformation having assigned base points on it.
gap or error: Singular original curves require the assigned-cluster convention; this is not a modern model-independent numerical class.
repair and reference: For a smooth rational curve of square ν≥0, blow up ν+1 points and contract its resulting −1 transform; Commentary I.11.
notes: The qualifier smooth-point neighborhood comes from the preceding definition.

statement (modern): Each of the 27 lines on a general smooth cubic surface is exceptional of the first kind.
repair and reference: On Bl₆P² the classes Eᵢ, H−Eᵢ−Eⱼ, 2H−Σ_(j≠i)Eⱼ have square −1 and anticanonical degree 1. Commentary I.11.
notes: The familiar plane representation of cubic surfaces is used, not proved on this page.

statement (modern): A plane representation of a smooth cubic surface can send any chosen line to one of the six base points' neighborhoods.
repair and reference: Choose a six-line exceptional configuration containing the chosen line and contract it; this is the classical cubic-surface representation assumed by Enriques.
notes: No specific earlier citation is printed beside this example; Conforto is a general prerequisite named in the preface.

statement (modern): The plane contains no first-kind exceptional curve.
repair and reference: Every nonzero degree-d plane curve has square d²>0, whereas a first-kind curve has square −1.
notes: Immediate once the forthcoming necessary numerical condition is known.

statement (modern): A line in the plane can be contracted by a quadratic homaloidal net with two base points on that line.
repair and reference: Its strict transform has square 1−1−1=−1; standard quadratic coordinates contract the line.
notes: The third quadratic base point lies off the line.

statement (modern): A smooth conic can be contracted by a homaloidal cubic net with one double and four simple base points on it.
gap or error: The centers must be suitably general; the double multiplicity belongs to the net, not to the conic.
repair and reference: Net type (3;2,1,1,1,1) has zero residual intersection with the conic; the conic's strict transform has square 4−5=−1. Commentary I.11.
notes: All five points count once in the conic's self-intersection drop.

statement (modern): The first-kind/second-kind distinction is relative to the surface model and need not survive birational maps with base points.
repair and reference: Blowing up points of a smooth rational curve lowers its square by one each time; the plane examples illustrate the change.
notes: No absolute birational invariant is claimed.

statement (modern): A second-kind curve can be represented as a first-kind curve on a suitable transformed model.
gap or error: A resolved graph may have a reducible exceptional fiber; identifying an individual component as first kind needs the full-neighborhood hypothesis.
repair and reference: For the intended elementary situation resolve assigned points and choose a sufficiently positive model separating the remaining curve; Commentary I.11.
notes: Do not replace this by the false rule that every component of any resolved exceptional fiber has square −1.

statement (modern): For the stated smooth-branch setup, the transforming system satisfies C·ω=i₁+⋯+i_s at its base points on ω.
gap or error: For a singular ω, the unweighted sum is incomplete.
repair and reference: General formula Σ iⱼ·mult_(pⱼ)(ωⱼ), summed over proper and infinitely near assigned centers. Commentary I.11.
notes: The source's formula tacitly uses multiplicity-one branches.

statement (modern): Adding a sufficiently positive base-point-free auxiliary system realizes a model retaining ω as a curve while the transformed original system contracts it.
gap or error: Multiplication of sections on the original X retains the original base ideal; graph resolution and positivity are needed.
repair and reference: Construct the resolved graph and choose an ample embedding so the relevant systems descend as morphisms. Commentary I.11.
notes: The source does not spell out these model choices.

statement (modern): Imposing a general simple base point on a sufficiently free system lowers its moving degree by one.
repair and reference: On the blowup, (π*C−E)²=C²−1.
notes: A completely arbitrary system must separate the relevant first-order directions; sufficiently general/positive choice supplies this.

statement (modern): A general curve through that smooth point meets the exceptional P¹ once.
notes: This is the intersection with the point's full infinitesimal neighborhood.

statement (modern): The degree equation n=(n−1)+ν+2 forces the exceptional self-intersection ν=−1.
repair and reference: Bilinearity applied to π*C=(π*C−E)+E.
notes: The displayed equation is correct.

statement (modern): The genus equation π=π+ρ+1−1 forces the exceptional virtual genus ρ=0.
repair and reference: Arithmetic-genus addition for E plus a unisecant residual curve.
notes: The displayed equation is correct.

statement (modern): The smooth point's exceptional neighborhood is rational.
repair and reference: The exceptional divisor of Bl_pX is P(T_pX)≅P¹; Stacks Project, Tag 0C2I.
notes: This also gives genus zero directly.

statement (modern): For the contracting system, a member through a point of E contains E and has residual curve meeting E once.
repair and reference: Pull back a general curve through the smooth target point; its total transform is E plus its strict transform.
notes: This alternative calculation reproduces ν=−1 and ρ=0.

statement (modern): An irreducible first-kind exceptional curve has virtual characters (p_a,E²)=(0,−1).
repair and reference: Blowup formulas or the two displayed sum calculations; Commentary I.11.
notes: Necessity is established here; sufficiency is anticipated on p. 36.

statement (modern): Second-kind curves have adjusted genus zero and nonnegative degree on the appropriate pre-contraction model.
gap or error: Unqualified p_a(original curve)=0 is false for a contractible nodal cubic; virtual assignment is essential.
repair and reference: Resolve the assigned singularity cluster first; a nodal plane cubic gives p_a=1 but adjusted genus 1−1=0. Commentary I.11.
notes: The p. 33 convention prevents an anachronistic reading of this assertion.

statement (modern): A ruling fiber has square zero.
repair and reference: Distinct fibers are disjoint and numerically equivalent, hence F²=0.
notes: The base of the ruling need not be rational.

statement (modern): A line in P² has square one.
repair and reference: Bézout / H²=1.
notes: Used as a second-kind numerical example.

statement (modern): A conic in P² has square four.
notes: Used as a second-kind numerical example.

statement (modern): An integral first-kind exceptional curve has no double or higher singular points.
repair and reference: Normalization gives p_a=g+Σδ=0; all δ vanish, so it is smooth rational. Beauville (2020), Lecture I, genus of a singular curve; Commentary I.11.
notes: This is correct; singularities of the ambient projective model are avoided on the smooth model.

statement (modern): An integral curve of arithmetic genus zero and self-intersection −1 contracts to a smooth point.
gap or error: The page explicitly postpones the effective extension of the systems and does not prove smoothness of the image point.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo contraction proof via ample H, exact sequences on E, Stein factorization, and the completed local ring. Stacks Project, Tags 0C2M and 0C2L; Commentary I.11.
notes: The theorem is true; the proof on these pages is incomplete by explicit design.

statement (modern): Adding E with E²=−1 to a system meeting it i times changes its intersection with E to i−1.
notes: Numerical step in the contraction sketch.

statement (modern): The degree of C+E is n+2i−1.
repair and reference: Expand (C+E)².
notes: Numerical step in the contraction sketch.

statement (modern): The arithmetic genus of C+E is π+i−1.
repair and reference: Use p_a(E)=0 in the sum formula.
notes: Numerical step in the contraction sketch.

statement (modern): Adding E increases degree minus twice genus by one.
notes: This alone does not imply the existence of new moving sections.

statement (modern): The addition of E genuinely enlarges the linear system and keeps an irreducible moving general member when the initial system is sufficiently general.
gap or error: Enriques explicitly refers forward for this cohomological/effectivity step.
repair and reference: Choose H very ample with H¹(H)=0; the sequence with quotient O_P¹(i−j) gives h⁰(H+jE)−h⁰(H+(j−1)E)=i−j+1 for j≤i. Commentary I.11; Stacks Tag 0C2M.
notes: It is a stated future dependency, not an attempted proof based only on arithmetic.

statement (modern): After i additions, |C+iE| is base-point-free and contracts E.
gap or error: Global generation and birational behavior are not deduced in the source.
repair and reference: Lift the generated restriction O_E(0) and use the original very ample sections off E. Commentary I.11; Stacks Tag 0C2M.
notes: Take the appropriate complete system on a sufficiently positive initial class.

statement (modern): The contracted point is smooth, so E is of the first kind.
gap or error: Zero intersection with a generated divisor alone does not prove a smooth image point.
repair and reference: Conormal quotients O_E(m), formal functions, and a regular completed local ring C[[u,v]]; Stacks Tag 0C2L.
notes: This is the decisive local step of Castelnuovo's criterion.

statement (modern): If Σiⱼ>2π−2−n for finitely many first-kind curves meeting C in iⱼ points, one obtains a system with N>2Π−2.
gap or error: The positive replacement of C must preserve the given inequality. Disjointness is needed for a simultaneous-blowdown interpretation, but not for the existence inequality.
repair and reference: Write G=ΣEⱼ−K_X, so the hypothesis is C·G>0. Since moving C is nef, take ample A, m≫0 with (mC+A)·G>0, and then H=t(mC+A) very ample with H¹(H)=0. Set iⱼ=H·Eⱼ and form D=H+ΣiⱼEⱼ by successive generated additions; cross terms cancel in −K_X·D=H·G>0. Commentary I.11.
notes: For disjoint curves the source's idea gives N=n+Σiⱼ² and Π=π+Σiⱼ(iⱼ−1)/2.

statement (modern): Existence of a moving irreducible system with N>2Π−2 characterizes the birationally ruled surfaces, including rational surfaces, over C.
gap or error: The classification implication is promised for later chapters and is outside the proof supplied here.
repair and reference: Adjunction gives K_X·D<0 for a nef moving class, forcing P_m=0 for all m; use the complex surface classification. Beauville (1996), classification and ruled-surface chapters.
notes: Do not claim pp. 1–40 prove the complete classification.

statement (modern): On a nonruled surface every resolved irreducible moving system satisfies n≤2π−2.
repair and reference: A nonzero pluricanonical effective divisor has nonnegative intersection with the moving nef class; adjunction gives the inequality. Commentary I.11.
notes: Uses existence of some pluricanonical section for a nonruled complex surface.

statement (modern): A nonruled surface has a birational smooth model with no exceptional curves in Enriques's smooth-point sense.
repair and reference: Contract −1-curves; the Picard number decreases and termination is finite. The second-kind phenomenon is excluded as below. Commentary I.11; Beauville (2020), Lecture II.
notes: The model may contain rational −2-curves contractible to singular points.

statement (modern): A surface containing a second-kind curve, in the smooth rational nonnegative-square model described, is birationally ruled.
gap or error: For a singular original curve one must first keep track of its assigned resolution and the intended model.
repair and reference: A smooth rational E with E²=ν≥0 is nef and K_X·E=−ν−2<0, so all plurigenera vanish. Commentary I.11.
notes: The text sketches this using repeated addition.

statement (modern): For a smooth rational curve of square ν≥0, repeated additions do not decrease the intersection of the resulting system with the curve.
repair and reference: (C+jE)·E=C·E+jν.
notes: Arithmetic monotonicity is correct.

statement (modern): Repeated additions eventually produce N>2Π−2.
gap or error: One must ensure the resulting effective divisors belong to generated irreducible systems.
repair and reference: With H sufficiently positive, restrictions on E stay nonnegative and H¹ vanishes inductively; (H+jE)²−2p_a(H+jE)+2=H²−2p_a(H)+2+j(ν+2). Commentary I.11.
notes: Supplies the effectivity behind the growth argument.

statement (modern): Distinct proper base points yield disjoint irreducible exceptional divisors on the corresponding resolved model.
gap or error: Arbitrary image embeddings can identify points; interpret this on the smooth resolution.
repair and reference: Blowups at distinct points have disjoint P¹ fibers. Commentary I.12.
notes: The system should be sufficiently positive to realize this model.

statement (modern): A base point of multiplicity i yields exceptional image of projective order i.
gap or error: The intersection L·E is the degree of the restricted bundle; it equals the degree of the projective image only when the map on E has degree one.
repair and reference: For L=π*A−iE, L·E=i=d·deg φ(E), where d is the degree of E→φ(E). Sufficient jet separation makes d=1 and realizes the expected projective order; positivity alone does not. Commentary I.12 and the mapping-degree qualification in §6.
notes: Projective order is distinct from self-intersection −1.

statement (modern): When O₁ specializes to a first-neighborhood point of O, Ω decomposes as ω+ω₁ and Ω₁=ω₁.
repair and reference: Total transform of the first exceptional divisor under the second blowup is its strict transform plus the new exceptional divisor.
notes: A precise blowup identity replaces the informal limiting language.

statement (modern): The two projective orders in that decomposition are i−i₁ and i₁.
gap or error: The two intersection degrees are unconditional; identifying them with projective image degrees again requires degree-one maps on both exceptional components.
repair and reference: Intersect L=π*A−iE₀*−i₁E₁* with the two strict exceptional curves. Each result is the map degree times the projective image degree. Sufficient jet separation gives the source’s asserted image degrees. Commentary I.12; compare §6.
notes: Positivity of differences is expressly assumed but does not, by itself, imply birationality of the component maps.

statement (modern): A cluster of points infinitely near O produces a connected reducible exceptional total divisor, containing the later exceptional cycles.
repair and reference: The exceptional fiber of a composite of point blowups is connected; successive total pullbacks give the stated cycles.
notes: Multiplicity is necessary at satellite points.

statement (modern): For a free chain O,O₁,…,O_s along a smooth branch, Ω=ω+ω₁+⋯+ω_s.
repair and reference: Each free blowup pulls back one multiplicity-one component; Commentary I.12.
notes: There are s+1 components.

statement (modern): The later total exceptional divisors are Ω_j=ω_j+⋯+ω_s.
repair and reference: Apply the same pullback calculation starting at the j-th blowup.
notes: Includes Ω_s=ω_s.

statement (modern): The free-chain restricted line-bundle degrees are i−i₁,i₁−i₂,…,i_s and telescope to i; Enriques identifies these with the projective orders.
gap or error: Each intersection degree equals the degree of the component map times its image degree. The printed image-degree interpretation and its unweighted telescoping sum require degree-one maps on all components.
repair and reference: For L=π*A−ΣmⱼEⱼ*, L·Eⱼ=mⱼ−m_(j+1) and L·E_s=m_s. If dⱼ is the degree of Eⱼ→φ(Eⱼ), then L·Eⱼ=dⱼ deg φ(Eⱼ). Sufficient jet separation gives dⱼ=1; positivity alone does not. Commentary I.12; compare §6.
notes: These restricted line-bundle degrees are distinct from the negative virtual degrees. Their sum is always i; the sum of image degrees equals i under the stated degree-one qualification.

statement (modern): The full cycles Ω_j, rather than arbitrary individual components, are exceptional neighborhoods of the original points.
repair and reference: Use total exceptional divisors; strict components may have square −2 or lower and do not individually contract to smooth points.
notes: The source explicitly distinguishes entire exceptional curves and components.

statement (modern): The free-chain configuration is produced by successive blowups at the indicated points.
gap or error: The printed sequence ends at F_s although O,…,O_s requires s+1 blowups; subsequent Fi indexing is shifted.
repair and reference: Use X₀→X₁→⋯→X_(s+1), with E_i created on X_(i+1). Commentary I.12.
notes: Source indexing slip verified in the scan.

statement (modern): For the free chain, each strict component meets its successor once and no other nonadjacent component.
repair and reference: Successive centers are free, not at preceding intersections; use the blowup graph rule.
notes: The last clause of the local construction makes this precise.

statement (modern): Each nonlast component has square −2; the last has square −1.
repair and reference: Each is born with square −1 and exactly one later free center lies on it.
notes: The source's geometric computation is correct apart from the surface-index shift.

statement (modern): The composite free-chain exceptional divisor has arithmetic genus zero.
gap or error: The displayed genus count uses +(s−1)−(s−1) despite s+1 components.
repair and reference: Correct formula Σ_(0..s)0+s−s=0; there are s edges. Commentary I.12.
notes: The result is correct; the displayed indexing is not.

statement (modern): The composite free-chain exceptional divisor has square −1.
gap or error: The displayed 2(s−1) gives the wrong edge count under the source's indexing.
repair and reference: Correct calculation s(−2)−1+2s=−1. Commentary I.12.
notes: This is a printed arithmetic/indexing slip, not an OCR error.

statement (modern): Every tail cycle Ω_j retains the same virtual characters (0,−1) as a single exceptional divisor.
repair and reference: It is a total pullback of a −1-curve; square and arithmetic genus are preserved under pullback.
notes: A direct argument removes dependence on an informal continuity principle.

statement (modern): Satellite configurations can make the total exceptional cycles nonreduced.
repair and reference: Blowing up an intersection adds the sum of the two existing coefficients to the new exceptional divisor.
notes: The following cusp example supplies the explanation.

statement (modern): For O,O₁,O₂ along a cuspidal branch, the satellite O₂ is the intersection of the strict first exceptional component with the second exceptional component.
repair and reference: This is the three-blowup model of the specified proximity pattern.
notes: The term satellite refers to proximity to two earlier points.

statement (modern): In the satellite specialization, the restricted line-bundle degrees on the first strict component and newest component are i−i₁−i₂ and i₂; Enriques calls these the projective orders.
gap or error: Identifying these intersection degrees with the projective image degrees requires the restrictions of the map to both components to have degree one.
repair and reference: The proximity formula gives L·E₀=m₀−m₁−m₂ and L·E₂=m₂. In general L·Eⱼ=dⱼ deg φ(Eⱼ), with dⱼ the degree of the component map. Sufficient separation gives dⱼ=1 and recovers the stated projective orders. Commentary I.12; compare §6.
notes: The loss of i₂ in the first component’s intersection degree is accounted for by the extra copy of the newest component in its total transform; this intersection identity does not require degree-one image maps.

statement (modern): The total exceptional divisor of O is Ω=ω+ω₁+2ω₂.
repair and reference: Three successive blowups give E₀* = E₀+E₁+2E₂; Commentary I.12.
notes: This displayed formula is correctly transcribed.

statement (modern): The new component must be doubled because the last blowup center is a double point of the previous total exceptional divisor.
gap or error: The prose prints transformed ω₁ where ω₂ is required.
repair and reference: Replace that component label by ω₂; the preceding sentence and p. 38 formula determine it uniquely.
notes: Scan-confirmed source slip.

statement (modern): The general multiplicities and connections are attributed to Barber and Zariski's 1935 work.
gap or error: Printed E. Barber should be S. F. Barber; the journal abbreviation Ann. Journ. is incorrect here.
repair and reference: Barber, S. F., & Zariski, O. (1935). Reducible exceptional curves of the first kind. American Journal of Mathematics,57(1),119–141. doi:10.2307/2372025.
notes: Bibliography verified; the full paper was not inspected in this audit.

statement (modern): The total exceptional divisor for O followed by s infinitely near points has s+1 irreducible components.
repair and reference: Each point blowup creates exactly one new exceptional component; later blowups preserve strict components.
notes: Counts the components of its total support.

statement (modern): The coefficient h_i of ω_i in Ω equals the minimum multiplicity at O of a branch passing through O₁,…,O_i.
gap or error: The statement uses branch/curvette conventions rather than arbitrary strict-transform multiplicities.
repair and reference: Use the recurrence for total-transform coefficients and a curvette transverse to E_i; intersection with a general line proves the minimum. Commentary I.12; Casas-Alvero (2000), chap. 3.
notes: Enriques quotes the rule without proof and attributes the analysis to Barber–Zariski.

statement (modern): The same multiplicity rule applies to Ω₁,…,Ω_s after making the corresponding infinitely near point proper.
repair and reference: Restart the curvette and total-transform calculation on the intermediate surface.
notes: Footnote (2) explains the proper-point convention.

statement (modern): The final component ω_i can meet ω_(i+t) rather than its chronological successor, according to the chain of centers proximate to O_i.
gap or error: The final graph must account for edges removed by satellite blowups; chronological order alone is insufficient.
repair and reference: At a free blowup append an edge; at an intersection blowup replace one edge by two. Commentary I.12.
notes: This is the precise operational interpretation of the source's proximity description.

statement (modern): If t later centers are proximate to O_i, the strict component has square −1−t.
repair and reference: E_i=E_i*−Σ_(p_j≻p_i)E_j*, with total-transform Gram matrix −I.
notes: One self-intersection unit is lost at each center on that strict component.

statement (modern): With their correct multiplicities, all total exceptional cycles Ω_i have square −1 and arithmetic genus zero.
repair and reference: Pullback preserves square and p_a; alternatively compute with the proximity matrix.
notes: Individual components need not have these characters.

statement (modern): The limiting union of the previously disjoint exceptional curves is Ω+Ω₁+⋯+Ω_s; each strict component's coefficient is the sum of its coefficients in these cycles.
repair and reference: Add total-transform divisor classes coefficient by coefficient.
notes: The present commentary additionally identifies this sum with K_Y−π*K_X; that identification is not claimed on this page.

statement (modern): An isolated curve of positive virtual degree has an intrinsic virtual characteristic series, independently of belonging to a positive-dimensional linear system.
gap or error: Positive degree does not by itself guarantee nonzero H⁰; n>0 is unnecessary for the normal-bundle definition.
repair and reference: The intrinsic complete series is |N_C/X|=|O_C(C)|, possibly empty. Commentary I.13.
notes: For singular Cartier divisors normal sheaf remains defined; effective zero-divisor interpretation needs care.

statement (modern): Choose an irreducible auxiliary |K| such that |C+K| has irreducible general member to construct the series by restriction.
repair and reference: For sufficiently large K=mH, the usual positivity theorems ensure this.
notes: Arbitrary small choices need not give the complete series.

statement (modern): The residual series cut on C by members of |C+K| through C∩K₀ has underlying line bundle O_C(C).
gap or error: The fixed intersection divisor must be removed; otherwise its degree is C²+C·K.
repair and reference: Tensor O_C(C+K) by O_C(−K₀); Commentary I.13.
notes: This explains the intended characteristic degree C².

statement (modern): The virtual characteristic series is independent of the auxiliary system.
gap or error: True for the intrinsic completed series or sufficiently positive auxiliaries; false as equality of every actual cut subseries under only the two stated irreducibility conditions.
repair and reference: Residual space V_K=ker(k_*δ), with δ:H⁰(N)→H¹(O_X); a sufficiently large K gives V_K=H⁰(N). Elliptic-product counterexample in Commentary I.13.
notes: The source's three-system comparison alone does not establish surjectivity.

statement (modern): An auxiliary K can always be chosen so that restriction from |C+K| to C is complete, giving the entire virtual characteristic series.
repair and reference: From 0→O_X(K)→O_X(C+K)→O_C(C+K)→0, Serre vanishing H¹(K)=0 gives surjectivity. Stacks Project, Tag 0B5U.
notes: Enriques expressly postpones the explanation of this sufficient-positivity assertion.

statement (modern): The virtual characteristic series is relevant to continuous families not confined to one linear-equivalence class.
repair and reference: The boundary H⁰(N)→H¹(O_X) records first-order variation of the line-bundle class; Commentary I.13.
notes: This anticipates the later Picard/irregularity theory without proving it here.

statement (modern): Infinitesimally neighboring members of a family cut some or all of the virtual characteristic series on C.
gap or error: No assertion that every first-order vector integrates, or that every family gives the complete series, follows.
repair and reference: T_[C]Div(X)=H⁰(C,N_C/X); characteristic divisors are zeros of the associated infinitesimal normal sections. Kleiman (2005), Remark 5.18; Commentary I.13.
notes: Obstructions and semiregularity are separate issues.

statement (modern): The virtual-character construction is attributed to Enriques's 1896 Introduzione, §§15–16.
repair and reference: Enriques, F. (1896). Introduzione alla geometria sopra le superficie algebriche. Memorie della Società Italiana delle Scienze detta dei XL,Series3,10,1–81.
notes: Bibliographic identity verified in the national-edition catalogue; those article sections were not independently inspected.

statement (modern): The virtual characteristic series definition is attributed to Severi's 1904 paper.
repair and reference: Severi, F. (1904). Osservazioni sui sistemi continui di curve appartenenti ad una superficie algebrica. Atti della Reale Accademia delle Scienze di Torino,39,376–392.
notes: Bibliography verified in Tannenbaum (1984), reference9; original paper text not inspected.

statement (modern): A Castelnuovo communication dated 25 December 1898, no.4, is said to contain the series implicitly.
gap or error: The specific communication was not independently located.
repair and reference: Retain as Enriques's reported attribution, not an independently verified priority claim.
notes: Source citation: Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo,25 Dec.1898,no.4.

statement (modern): The surface of unordered pairs of points of a genus-two curve supplies the cited historical example.
gap or error: Historical iperellittica does not mean the modern bielliptic-surface class.
